faqs.q: How much does a Lagotto Romagnolo cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $800–$3,000 for a Lagotto Romagnolo puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Lagotto Romagnolo?
faqs.a: Budget $150–$300 per month for a Lagotto Romagnolo, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Mid-size breeds sit in the moderate cost range across most ownership categories.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Lagotto Romagnolo?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($500–900), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($$400–$1,200 per year). Grooming adds $400–$1,200 annually for Lagotto Romagnolos due to their coat type.

faqs.q: How much does a Lagotto Romagnolo cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Lagotto Romagnolo are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,000–$4,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Lagotto Romagnolo?
faqs.a: Lagotto Romagnolos need brushing 3–4 times per week to prevent matting.  Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Lagotto Romagnolos shed a lot?
faqs.a: Lagotto Romagnolos shed minimally. A weekly brush is usually sufficient.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Lagotto Romagnolo need?
faqs.a: A wide-tooth comb, pin brush, and detangling spray are the core tools for a Lagotto Romagnolo's curly coat. Add a nail grinder and ear cleaner for complete at-home maintenance.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Lagotto Romagnolo?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Lagotto Romagnolos that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Lagotto Romagnolos easy to train?
faqs.a: Lagotto Romagnolos are considered easier to train than average — they respond quickly to reward-based methods and generalise cues well. Short 10–15 minute sessions outperform long correction-heavy drills.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Lagotto Romagnolo?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Lagotto Romagnolos. Keep sessions short and positive, end on a success, and vary your rewards to maintain engagement.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Lagotto Romagnolo?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Lagotto Romagnolo?
faqs.a: Most Lagotto Romagnolos learn basic obedience cues (sit, stay, come, down) within 2–4 weeks of daily practice. Reliable recall in distracting environments typically takes 2–3 months of consistent reinforcement.

faqs.q: What health problems do Lagotto Romagnolos commonly have?
faqs.a: Lagotto Romagnolos are most commonly associated with hip dysplasia. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Lagotto Romagnolos live?
faqs.a: Lagotto Romagnolos have an average lifespan of 15–17 years. Good nutrition, appropriate exercise, weight management and regular vet visits are the key factors in achieving the upper end of this range.

faqs.q: Are Lagotto Romagnolos prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Lagotto Romagnolos have a moderate-to-elevated risk of hip dysplasia, particularly for large or active breeds. Ask for OFA or PennHIP hip evaluation certificates when buying from a breeder. Weight control and avoiding high-impact exercise during bone growth (under 18 months) reduces risk.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Lagotto Romagnolo puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Lagotto Romagnolo puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Lagotto Romagnolo-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Lagotto Romagnolos good with kids?
faqs.a: Lagotto Romagnolos are generally known for being friendly and patient, making them well-suited to family life with children. Supervision is always recommended with young children regardless of breed — interactions should be taught from both sides.

faqs.q: Do Lagotto Romagnolos get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Lagotto Romagnolos are generally sociable with other dogs, particularly when well-socialised from puppyhood. Introduce new dogs on neutral territory and keep initial meetings brief and positive.

faqs.q: Do Lagotto Romagnolos bark a lot?
faqs.a: Lagotto Romagnolos are not considered excessive barkers. They may alert to strangers or unusual sounds, but are generally manageable with basic training. Consistent "quiet" reinforcement from puppyhood keeps this in check.

faqs.q: Are Lagotto Romagnolos good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Lagotto Romagnolos can live in apartments if their exercise needs are met consistently. The key variable is owner commitment to daily walks and enrichment — breed size alone doesn't determine apartment suitability.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Lagotto Romagnolo need per day?
faqs.a: Lagotto Romagnolos need approximately 45–60 minutes of exercise daily. A structured morning walk and an evening sniff walk usually cover their needs. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Lagotto Romagnolos good running partners?
faqs.a: Lagotto Romagnolos can join you for moderate runs once fully grown. They're better suited to steady 3–5 mile runs than extended distance. Watch for signs of fatigue and always run in cooler hours during summer.

faqs.q: What happens if a Lagotto Romagnolo doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Lagotto Romagnolos are less demanding than high-energy breeds, but chronic under-exercise still leads to weight gain and low-level restlessness. Even lower-energy breeds benefit from a consistent daily walk for both physical health and mental stimulation.

faqs.q: Can a Lagotto Romagnolo be off-lead?
faqs.a: Off-lead freedom for a Lagotto Romagnolo depends on recall reliability, not breed alone. Train recall from puppyhood using long-line sessions before progressing to full off-lead. A standard 20-foot long-line gives freedom while maintaining safety during the training phase.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Lagotto Romagnolo?
faqs.a: A Lagotto Romagnolo needs approximately 1½–3 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Lagotto Romagnolo?
faqs.a: Adult Lagotto Romagnolos should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Lagotto Romagnolo?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Medium-energy Lagotto Romagnolos do well on standard adult maintenance formulas with named protein as the first ingredient.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Lagotto Romagnolo from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Most Lagotto Romagnolos can transition to adult food between 12 and 15 months. Transition gradually over 7–10 days — mix 25% new food with 75% old food and shift the ratio every 2 days to avoid digestive upset.

faqs.q: Is a Lagotto Romagnolo a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Lagotto Romagnolos are generally considered suitable for first-time owners. They're responsive to training, manageable in size, and adaptable to different home environments. A puppy class is still recommended to build a strong foundation.

faqs.q: Are Lagotto Romagnolos good family dogs?
faqs.a: Lagotto Romagnolos are typically affectionate family dogs that do well with children and adapt to household routines. Their sociable nature means they prefer company over isolation.

faqs.q: Do Lagotto Romagnolos do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Lagotto Romagnolos form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Lagotto Romagnolo?
faqs.a: Plan for 1.5–2 hours per day dedicated to your Lagotto Romagnolo — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction. Add 15–30 minutes for grooming 3–4 times weekly. The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
